question: I submitted my PGWP application in October 2024. Do I have to show language test results?

question: Can I take my whole program online from outside Canada and still be eligible for a PGWP?

question: I studied 4 months at a school that isn't a DLI and then 6 months at a DLI. Can I get a PGWP?
answer: No, you cannot get a PGWP. The length of your studies must be at least 8 months for you to be eligible. Since you only spent 6 months at the DLI, you do not meet the eligibility requirement. (Source: Post-graduation work permit: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/eligibility.html)

question: My study permit had already expired when I applied for my PGWP. Can I work while I wait for the decision?
answer: Yes, you can work while waiting for the decision on your PGWP application if you had a valid study permit at the time you submitted your application, completed your study program, and were eligible to work off campus without a work permit while studying and you didn’t work more hours than you were allowed to. question: My scholarship covers only my tuition. Is that enough proof of funds for my study permit?
answer: No, a scholarship that covers only tuition is not enough proof of funds for your study permit. You must also show proof that you have sufficient funds to cover living expenses and transportation costs for the full duration of your studies. (Source: Study permit: Get the right documents - Proof of financial support, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html)

question: I'm 60 years old. Do I have to take the Canadian citizenship test?

question: After I become a citizen, can I travel abroad and come back to Canada using my old PR card?
answer: No, you cannot travel abroad and come back to Canada using your old PR card after becoming a citizen. Once you become a citizen, you should apply for a Canadian passport to travel abroad. If you have a valid or expired PR card, you can use it to prove your permanent resident status while your application is being processed. However, after becoming a citizen, you should not use your PR card to travel abroad. (Source: Canadian citizenship for adults and minor children: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/adult-minor/who.html)

question: Can I get a Canadian visitor visa when I land at the airport in Canada?
answer: No, you cannot get a Canadian visitor visa when you land at the airport in Canada. A valid Temporary Resident Visa is not a guarantee of entry into Canada. An officer at the port of entry will decide if you still meet the requirements for admission when you arrive. (Source: Guide 5256 - Applying for a visitor visa (temporary resident visa) - paper application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/guide-5256-applying-visitor-visa-temporary-resident-visa.html)

question: I hold Canadian citizenship but I work in Dubai right now. Is it possible for me to sponsor my wife for permanent residence?
